advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope warn_if_cache_write_never_read to a single run's rows (or document/rename that summarize evaluates it over the entire process-level usage-log file, not one run).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:479-487: `rows = _read(path)` then `warn_if_cache_write_never_read(rows, model=str(rows[0].get("model", "?")))`

src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:9-11: "when it points at a path, :func:`record` appends one JSON object per LLM call (JSONL). :func:`summarize` folds that file into a Markdown table" — the file spans the whole job, not one run
src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py: docstring of cache_write_never_read says 'True when a RUN's caching calls all WROTE the cache and NONE ever READ it' — the scope passed in is not one run
src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:487: `warn_if_cache_write_never_read(rows, model=str(rows[0].get("model", "?")))`
src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:526-528: `model = str(row.get("model"))` / `rollup = per_model.setdefault(model, ...)` — rows carry per-row models and the summary rolls up multiple models
advisory.finding: warn_if_cache_write_never_read is called from usage_log.summarize over the whole usage-log file, but its logic and warning are framed as 'a RUN's caching calls'. The usage log is a process-level append-only JSONL that accumulates every LLM call across a job (multiple gate runs, multiple operations), so the write-every-call/never-read predicate is evaluated across unrelated runs — potentially masking a genuinely-warm run mixed with cold ones, or attributing the shape to a scope the operator never reasons about as one run.
merged_from: The warn_if_cache_write_never_read call in summarize labels the warning with only the first row's model (rows[0].get('model')), but summarize itself builds a per-model rollup because a usage-log file mixes models. When the caching calls that triggered the shape are on a different model than rows[0], the warning names the wrong model.
scenarios: A CI job runs several plan-reviews plus other LLM operations; summarize folds all rows so the aggregate predicate reasons across operations that never shared a cache prefix.

scenarios: The code-grounded Pass-2 verifier runs agentic with tools; the dynamic remainder instruction interacts with the tool loop and multi-step message assembly, a path never asserted byte-identical.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting RunnerAgentStep-built RunRequest.cache_prefix equals shared_prefix for a plan-review verify step (and stays None for a non-prefix step).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py:326: `cache_prefix = ( shared_prefix if isinstance(shared_prefix, str) and shared_prefix and system_prompt.startswith(shared_prefix) ... else None )`
grep `.cache_prefix` across tests returns only test_cache_prefix_breakpoint.py:10 (a docstring) — no test reads req.cache_prefix off a RunnerAgentStep-built RunRequest
tests/unit/test_prompt_cache_split.py:193-201 captures runner.reqs but asserts only system_prompt and instructions, not r1.cache_prefix
advisory.finding: The new cache_prefix derivation in runs.py._build_run_request (isinstance/startswith/len guard producing RunRequest.cache_prefix) has no test asserting the resulting RunRequest.cache_prefix value. The existing test that drives this path (test_verify_step_system_prompt_is_plan_bearing) captures the RunRequest but only asserts system_prompt/instructions, never cache_prefix — so a regression that failed to set cache_prefix, or set it wrongly, would not be caught.
scenarios: A refactor drops the cache_prefix kwarg on the RunRequest returned by _build_run_request
The startswith/len guard is inverted or off-by-one so cache_prefix is None for a valid verify step
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_prompt_cache_split.py or test_shared_prefix.py, capture the RunRequest and assert `r1.cache_prefix == alpha` for the verify step, plus a case where shared_prefix is absent/not-a-prefix asserting `cache_prefix is None`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting the Pass-1 finder's RunRequest.cache_prefix equals prompts.shared_plan_prefix(plan).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:322: `cache_prefix=prompts.shared_plan_prefix(plan),`

No test in the diff or existing suite captures the finder's RunRequest to assert its cache_prefix; test_prompt_cache_split.py:84 (test_bespoke_plan_review_path_strips_marker...) asserts only system_prompt bytes, not cache_prefix
advisory.finding: The Pass-1 finder now sets cache_prefix=prompts.shared_plan_prefix(plan) on its RunRequest (passes.py:322), but no test asserts the finder's RunRequest carries that cache_prefix. A regression removing/mis-deriving the finder's cache_prefix — the WRITE side that must align with the verifier's READ boundary — would go undetected.
scenarios: A refactor of build_finder_request drops the cache_prefix kwarg
shared_plan_prefix(plan) for the finder diverges from the verifier's prefix, misaligning the breakpoint

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting estimate_marked_prefix_tokens is called with the cache_prefix span (not the full system prompt) when RunRequest.cache_prefix is a proper prefix, and with the full system prompt otherwise.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/runner.py:533-539: `system_prompt=( req.cache_prefix if req.cache_prefix and req.system_prompt.startswith(req.cache_prefix) and len(req.cache_prefix) < len(req.system_prompt) else req.system_prompt )`
search for `estimate_marked_prefix_tokens` under tests/ returns no matches — the new cache_prefix-vs-full-system branch is unexercised
src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:632: `return est_tokens(system_prompt)` — the value fed to warn_if_cache_ineffective depends on which span is passed
advisory.finding: The runner.py change to estimate_marked_prefix_tokens — selecting req.cache_prefix as the marked span (instead of the full system_prompt) when it is a proper prefix — has no test. This telemetry-accuracy path decides whether warn_if_cache_ineffective sees the correct marked-prefix token count; a regression using the full system prompt (over-counting the marked span) would silently suppress or distort the cache-floor warning.
scenarios: A refactor drops the cache_prefix branch, so the estimate uses the whole (larger) system prompt
The proper-prefix guard is inverted, over- or under-counting the marked tokens fed to the cache-floor warning
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert est_tokens(cache_prefix) == estimate_marked_prefix_tokens(anthropic_settings, system_prompt=cache_prefix) < estimate_marked_prefix_tokens(anthropic_settings, system_prompt=cache_prefix+suffix), and cover the runner branch by driving a real run with a cache_prefix set and spying the marked span, or extract the span-selection into a helper and unit-test it directly.
